messages:
maria_prod: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for Dedicated capacity SLA/throughput choices. Need to decide guaranteed vs best-effort, burst semantics, preemption rules, autoscale targets, and acceptance criteria. Tagging @ajay_eng @claire_sre @samir_infra @kevin_sales for input.
ajay_eng: +1. We should separate contract-level guarantees (committed tokens/sec/nodes) from operational SLOs (latency, availability).
claire_sre: Agree. Also need explicit preemption behavior: what gets evicted when demand > reserved? Per-customer fairness? priority tiers?
samir_infra: Two high-level options from infra pov: (A) hard reservations -> strict isolation but low global utilization; (B) soft reservations -> allow controlled burst using warm spare pool, preemptable when global contention high.
kevin_sales: Customers are asking for p95 latency guarantees (around 200–300ms) and the ability to burst for short windows. They care about predictable billing if we restrict bursts.
maria_prod: Draft acceptance criteria idea below — feedback welcome.
```
SLA / Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Commitment: customer reserves N nodes / X tokens/sec (committed_capacity).
- Availability: committed_capacity must be available >= 99.0% over billing month (measured p99 availability of nodes).
- Latency SLOs: for seq <= 512, p95 gen latency <= 250ms on committed instances.
- Throughput: sustained throughput delivered = committed_tokens_per_sec +/- 5% over 10m windows.
- Burst: allow burst up to 2x committed_capacity for up to 5 minutes every 30 minutes (configurable per contract). Bursts are best-effort beyond those windows.
- Preemption: burst-best-effort can be preempted if cluster_utilization_15m > 85%. Preemption order: transient workloads -> ephemeral jobs -> reserved customer burst.
- Fallback: if preempted, auto-fallback to smaller model variant (e.g., from gpt-q8 to gpt-q4b) within 10s where allowed by customer policy.
- Penalty: credits issued if Availability < SLA threshold (credit schedule to be defined).
```
ajay_eng: A few nitpicks: measure latency at the router edge (after routing, before tokenization) and state the test workload (tokens/sec distribution). We also need an explicit SLO delta for fallback (e.g., expected quality drop tolerances).
claire_sre: How do we detect cluster_utilization_15m robustly? Suggest metric: avg_gpu_utilization_15m or queue_length_15m > threshold. Also specify alerting playbook.
samir_infra: From infra side I propose these autoscale knobs: 
- min_nodes = committed_nodes
- warm_pool = max(ceil(0.1 * committed_nodes), 1)
- scale_up_timeout = 45s (target to add capacity)
- scale_down_hysteresis = 10m
These keep cold-starts predictable for committed customers.
kevin_sales: Important commercial question: how to price burst? Two options: included short bursts up to X per month, or per-token premium for burst beyond commitment. Sales prefers predictable included bursts for enterprise deals.
liz_ce: Note from CE: some regulated customers require non-preemptible capacity. We need to call out Private deployments vs Hosted Dedicated behavior.
maria_prod: Good point — propose private deployments be allowed non-preemptible by default. Hosted Dedicated offers preemptible burst for efficiency unless customer pays for a non-preemptible tier.
claire_sre: Also add acceptance tests for canary failover: simulate 20% of nodes lost in a pool and ensure traffic reroutes within 30s with degraded latency tracked.
ajay_eng: For model-level fallbacks we should publish an expected degradation matrix: e.g., smaller model -> 10–20% quality regression on rouge/utility for our eval set. This feeds into customer-facing docs.
samir_infra: Operational runbook sketch: 
1) Detection: cluster_utilization_5m > 95% or queue_latency_1m > 500ms -> trigger
2) Action: throttle best-effort traffic, enable burst preemption, spin warm_pool nodes if available
3) Escalation: if sustained > 10m, engage SRE oncall and notify product/sales for potential customer credits
4) Rollback: restore traffic and mark incident for postmortem
kevin_sales: Can we add a simple matrix in PRD mapping commitment tier -> allowed burst policy -> price multiplier? Sales needs that for term sheets.
maria_prod: Yes — I'll draft a commitment vs burst vs price table in the PRD. Also need explicit launch criteria: 
- Canary PASS (latency/throughput within 10% of expected on k=5 customers)
- Runbook complete and tested in staging
- Pricing table approved by finance
- Customer-facing docs + CE runbook ready
deploy-bot: PRD draft created: https://redwood.app/drive/d/prd-dedicated-slas-2259 (auto-tagged @maria_prod)
claire_sre: 👍 please add acceptance test IDs so we can automate during release.
maria_prod: I'll open a PR with the draft by EOD and tag reviewers. If no objections, target ship to beta next sprint.
kevin_sales: tagging @liz_ce for customer comms after PRD final.
liz_ce: I'll prepare a short FAQ for enterprise customers about preemption and non-preemptible private options.
maria_prod: Thanks everyone — expecting sign-offs by Wed so we can freeze acceptance criteria.
